commands.author: Pick-cat

target.title: fix(discord): bound gateway metadata response reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an unbounded `response.arrayBuffer()` read in the Discord gateway metadata fetch path. The `materializeGuardedResponse()` helper clones the SSRF-guarded response body by reading the entire stream into memory with no byte cap, so a hostile or misconfigured upstream endpoint returning a large payload can exhaust the gateway process heap (OOM). The same helper is used for every gateway info lookup and metadata-bearing HTTP request in the Discord plugin.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the unbounded `response.arrayBuffer()` with `readResponseWithLimit` capped at 64 KiB — more than enough for the `/gateway/bot` JSON payload (typically < 1 KiB). This matches the bounded-read pattern already deployed in `extensions/discord/src/internal/rest.ts` (8 MiB cap, PR #97693) and across the broader codebase (Signal, Inworld, Matrix, etc.). No new dependency or config knob.

## User Impact

A compromised or misconfigured Discord API endpoint can no longer OOM the gateway process through the gateway metadata fetch path. Normal Discord gateway operation is unaffected — the 64 KiB cap is ~60× the typical payload size.

## Real behavior proof

Proof script drives `readResponseWithLimit` (the SDK helper used by `materializeGuardedResponse`) against a real `node:http` server. Same script includes a negative control that reproduces the unbounded `response.arrayBuffer()` behavior pre-fix.

**Environment:** Linux, Node 24, `node --import tsx proof-discord-gateway-bound.mts`

```
[case 1] readResponseWithLimit: 200-byte payload under 65536-byte cap
  ok: returns Buffer
  ok: payload round-trips
  ok: body length (46 B) <= cap (65536 B)
  wall: 7.8ms | body: 46 bytes

[case 2] readResponseWithLimit: 100000-byte payload over 65536-byte cap
  ok: throws on oversized response
  ok: error message contains cap size
  wall: 1.7ms | error: Content too large: 100000 bytes (limit: 65536 bytes)

[case 3] NEGATIVE CONTROL: unbounded response.arrayBuffer() vs bounded reader
  ok: unbounded read consumes all 100000 bytes
  unbounded: wall=1.5ms | body=100000 bytes | cap=none → OOM risk on large payloads
  ok: bounded read throws instead of consuming full body
  bounded:   wall=1.0ms | stopped at 65536-byte cap → safe

=== Proof Summary ===
cap: 65536 bytes (64 KiB)
oversized payload: 100000 bytes (1.5× cap)
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 7 passed, 0 failed
```

**What was not tested:** A live Discord bot token was not available, so the full `fetchDiscordGatewayInfo → fetchDiscordGatewayMetadataGuarded` chain against `api.discord.com` could not be exercised end-to-end. The tested surface (`readResponseWithLimit` at the 64 KiB cap) is the exact mechanism added by this change; the SSRF guard and transport layers above it are unchanged.

## Evidence

### Vitest regression tests (real production functions with mocked SSRF guard)

```
pnpm test extensions/discord/src/monitor/gateway-metadata.bound.test.ts        extensions/discord/src/monitor/gateway-metadata.test.ts
```

```
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  5 passed (5)
```

- **under-cap**: small valid gateway payload → `response.ok === true`, body round-trips
- **over-cap**: 100 KB response → `rejects.toThrow(/Discord gateway metadata response exceeds/)`
- **boundary**: 60 KB padding payload under 64 KiB cap → body round-trips
- **existing tests**: timeout resolution and fallback behavior unchanged (2 tests)

### Negative control (vitest, same environment)

Reverted `materializeGuardedResponse` to `origin/main` (unbounded `response.arrayBuffer()`):

```
 FAIL  rejects response body exceeding 64 KiB with an overflow error
AssertionError: promise resolved "Response { status: 200, ... }" instead of rejecting
```

Old code silently returns the full 100 KB body instead of throwing — confirming the unbounded read.
